subject: environmental-science

moments.title: Six IPCC Assessment cycles
moments.body: AR1 (1990): warming 'could be largely due to natural variability'. AR2 (1995): 'discernible human influence'. AR3 (2001): 'most of the warming over the last 50 years is likely to have been due to'. AR4 (2007): 'very likely'. AR5 (2013-14): 'extremely likely'. AR6 (2021-23): 'unequivocal' that human influence has warmed the climate.
moments.takeaway: The IPCC's escalating certainty across 33 years tracks both improving science and the difficulty of conveying consensus to policymakers.

now.title: Climate assessment today
now.body: The IPCC's AR7 cycle is underway (2024-2030). The Special Reports — SR1.5 (2018), SRCCL (2019, land), SROCC (2019, ocean and cryosphere) — proved increasingly influential. IPCC reports are now central inputs to COP negotiations.
now.open_questions: How does the IPCC handle accelerating non-linear changes (tipping points)? AR6 increased emphasis but more is needed.

reflection: The IPCC does not conduct research; it synthesises. Its statements are negotiated word by word in governmental approval sessions. The line between scientific summary and political compromise is real.
